units.text: INT. ABANDONED PLANETARIUM - NIGHT
A great domed ceiling, plaster cracked like dry riverbed.
Rows of reclining seats, all tilted toward a sky that no longer exists.
Dust hangs in a single shaft of moonlight from a broken skylight.
INSPECTOR MIRELLA STROZZI, 50s, charcoal overcoat, white glove on one hand, kneels at the base of the star projector, a black iron dumbbell of a machine.
She sets a small cassette recorder on the floor and presses play.
Entry one. The caretaker was found here, third seat, row nine, facing south. No wound. No struggle. Only the projector, warm to the touch, though power has been cut for eleven years.
units.name: STROZZI

units.text: She stops the tape.
Lifts a lens cap.
Underneath, a thumbprint in fresh grease.
Slowly she stands, looks up at the dead dome.
The cracks branch like constellations nobody named.
Warm.
units.name: STROZZI

units.text: She presses record.
Speaks into the recorder.
Entry two. Someone has been drawing the stars back in.
units.name: STROZZI

units.text: Above her, tiny pinpricks of white chalk dot the plaster.
Hundreds.
Fresh.
The projector clicks.
